copy: Fashion Week is not one stimulus. RN Collins separates nine evidence-bounded pathways—sleep opportunity, light, sound, crowds, attention, social evaluation, movement, fatigue and recovery—without inventing a Fashion Week brain. Official BFC media are embedded with permission boundaries; every scientific source carries a transfer limit.

The invitation says one event. Your nervous system gets a clock, a room, a crowd, cameras, sound, light, movement and recovery. No study establishes a Fashion Week-specific circuit. The more useful question is which conditions were present—and which findings actually transfer.
Fashion Week tired is real. It is not automatically a diagnosis—and a runway spotlight is not a scientific dose.

Fashion Week is usually documented as spectacle. I rebuilt it as an exposure-and-labor question. Nine claims separate what sleep, light, sound, crowd, social-stress and standing research can support from what the event footage cannot prove. The result is an exhibition plus a no-storage field mapper—not a wellness score.
Fashion Week is not one stimulus. It is a stack of clocks, rooms, sound, light, bodies, cameras, judgment, labor and recovery. A 9-part evidence fitting:

Overwhelmed, exhilarated and exhausted are descriptions. None is a brain scan. Fashion Week can be all three; the science gets useful only when we separate the conditions and keep every transfer limit visible.

A field guide to event intensity: what controlled studies of sleep loss, timed light, sound, crowds, social evaluation and prolonged standing can suggest—and why none measures Fashion Week as a single nervous-system exposure.
